previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder and recent bereavement was admitted at 35 weeks for recurrent severe depression and akathisia, requiring continuation of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) during pregnancy. She was found to have new-onset hypothyroidism, which was treated with levothyroxine. After several ECT sessions with good psychiatric response, she developed gestational hypertension and signs of preeclampsia, prompting induction of labor. She delivered a healthy infant via spontaneous vaginal delivery after a prolonged induction, with manual extraction of a retained placenta. Her postpartum course was uncomplicated, with resolution of psychiatric symptoms and stable vital signs. She was discharged home on quetiapine, levothyroxine, and prenatal vitamins, with plans for ongoing outpatient ECT and psychiatric follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms ___ presented to gyn triage on postpartum day 7 on 
___ for severe range blood pressures ranging in the 
160-180s/80-100s. While in triage, she received 20mg IV 
labetalol x2 to quickly bring blood pressure down, and she 
responded well. HELLP labs were sent that were within normal 
limits. Patient also received Nifedipine 30mg CR before being 
transferred to the postpartum floor for further management, 
which she responded well to. Upon arrival, patient also had 
persistent headache that improved as blood pressures decreased. 

On the floor, patient was continued on Nifedipine 30mg CR daily, 
and pressures remained stable in the 120/60s. Her continued with 
an intermittent headache that was palliated with fioricet. 

By hospital day 2, patient was feeling well, with blood 
pressures well controlled and stable. Headache controlled with 
oral pain medications prn. Patient was then discharged home in 
stable condition with outpatient follow up scheduled. Her ECT 
treatment that was originally scheduled for day of discharge was 
postponed until the next week. Patient was aware and in 
agreement.
